lockMeans: The lock keeps everything encrypted and safe.
yourKeyStaysOn: Your messages, pictures, videos, voice messages and files are locked (encrypted) before they are saved, so only you and your friends can open them. Not even we can. The lock is made by itself on this device and stays here. In a browser the lock is weaker than in the app, because the web page is loaded from our server each time.
waitingForAccessTo: Waiting for access to your old messages and files.
removeNeedsApproval: This device is not approved yet, so it cannot remove other devices. Approve it from one of your approved devices first.
aRemovedKeyIs: A removed key is deleted. Nothing new is locked for it, and old items lose their copy for it the next time they are locked again. The device also gets no more notifications from your account.
useThisIfYou: Use this if you lost your rescue words, or if you suspect this device. This device gets a new lock and 24 new rescue words. Your old messages and files are moved to the new lock first, then the old lock is removed. Old items are not locked again with the new lock yet: if the old lock was stolen, it could still open what was locked for it.
typeTheRecoveryWords: Type the 24 rescue words you wrote down. The lock is then put back on this device.
thatDidNotWork: That did not work. Try again.
couldNotBeOpened: {{ skipped }} could not be opened on this device. Try again on the device where that key lives.
doneTheOtherDevice: Done. The other device can now open your old messages and files.
theKeyCouldNot: The lock could not be removed.
theKeyCouldNot2: The lock could not be restored.
doneYourHistoryIs: Done. Your history is open on this device.
someThingsAreLocked: Some of your old messages and files are locked on this device.
lockedCounts: {{ messages }} messages and {{ files }} files are locked on this device. Open them again with your other device, your rescue words or a friend.
thisDeviceHasNoWorking: This device has no working lock.
theKeyOnThisNever: The lock on this device is not saved on the server (it was never saved, or it was removed from another of your devices), so it does not count.
thisDeviceHasNoKey: Your account has locks on other devices, but this device has none.
soYourOldMessages: Your old messages and files stay locked here until it has one. Open them with your rescue words, or turn on the lock and ask your other devices or a friend.
myOtherDevices: Another phone or computer of mine
waitingForYourOther: Waiting for one of your other devices to say Approve.
yourOtherDeviceIs: Your other device is opening your history for this one.
addedOfTotal: {{ added }} of {{ total }} done. Keep the app open on both devices.
oneOfYourOther: One of your other devices said it was not you, and removed the lock of this device. Use your rescue words, or ask a friend.
askYourOtherDevices: Ask your other devices to open your old messages for this one. A card shows on them (and a message, when they are closed).
noOtherDeviceHas: No other device of yours has a lock. Use your rescue words or ask a friend.
aFriendCanOpen: A friend can open what you shared with them and lock it again for you on this device. Ask one friend at a time.
noFriendsInThis: No friends in this circle yet.
openTheAppOn: Open Seven Friends on one of these devices (it must be logged in and show the same account). A banner asks you to Approve. It does not matter which one.
noRescueCodeText: Your rescue words are 24 words on paper. If you lose every phone and computer of yours, they are the only way to open your old messages and files on a new device. It takes a moment.
lockingOldThings: Locking your older messages and notes with the new lock. You can keep using the app.
someCouldNotBeLocked: Some older items could not be opened on this device. Open the app on another device of yours to finish them.
removeFromAnother: To remove this device, open Seven Friends on another device of yours.
howApprovalWorksText: “Not approved yet” means no other device of yours has said Approve for it, so it cannot open your old messages and files. To approve it, open Seven Friends on another device of yours that is already approved (it has no badge) and is logged in to the same account. A banner “A new device wants to join your lock” shows there: press Approve. If no device is approved, use your 24 rescue words instead.
startOverTitle: I lost my devices and my rescue words
startOverText: This starts your lock over with this device. Every other device of yours is removed. Each of your friends is asked to confirm that it is really you, and can then help you open your old messages again.
startOverFailed: Could not start over. Check the connection and try again.
whyRecoverTitle: Why do I need to do this?
whyRecoverText: Your old messages and files are locked. The lock that opens them is on your old phone or computer, not on this one, and we cannot open them for you. Let another device, your 24 rescue words or a friend give this device access.
strongNoLockedMessages: No locked messages on this device. Nothing needs to be recovered.
makeFailed: The lock could not be made on this device: {{ error }}
